title: Anisotropic bond-current susceptibilities and real-space current topology in correlated electron systems
abstract: We derive all symmetry-allowed bond-current form factors generated by nearest-neighbor bond-charge interactions on square, triangular, and kagome lattices. We find that the anisotropy of the bond-current susceptibility systematically favors ordering wave vectors that support closed loop-current states, whereas symmetry-related wave vectors with weaker susceptibility generate noncirculating current textures. Near van Hove filling, this correspondence is robust across all lattice geometries considered, producing staggered flux phases on the square lattice, diamond-shaped current patterns on the triangular lattice and both chiral and nonchiral loop-current states on the kagome lattice. Our results establish a direct link between bond-current form factors, susceptibility anisotropy, and real-space current topology, providing a general framework for identifying loop-current orders and interpreting signatures of time-reversal symmetry breaking in correlated electron materials.
summary: This work develops a general theoretical framework connecting bond-current susceptibility anisotropy to the resulting current topology in correlated electron materials. By analyzing three different lattices, the authors show that fluctuations near specific filling levels favor distinct real-space current patterns, such as closed loop currents or source–sink textures. This provides a powerful tool for interpreting experimental signatures of charge order and broken symmetries.
main_problem: To establish a direct link between bond-current form factors, susceptibility anisotropy, and the resulting real-space current topology in correlated electron systems.
main_result: The anisotropy of the bond-current susceptibility systematically favors ordering wave vectors that support closed loop-current states, providing a general framework for identifying such orders.
method: Derivation of symmetry-allowed bond-current form factors and calculation of the Random-Phase-Approximation (RPA) susceptibility on various lattices.
model_or_system: Correlated electron systems modeled using nearest-neighbor bond-charge interactions, studied on square, triangular, and kagome lattices.
key_observables: Bond-current form factors ($\gamma_k$), susceptibility anisotropy $\chi(Q)$, and real-space current topology (e.g., closed loop currents vs. source–sink textures).
important_parameters: Filling level ($\mu/t$), lattice geometry (square, triangular, kagome), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The physical current is identified with the imaginary part of the reconstructed order parameter; analysis often focuses on the sine-form-factor representation despite acknowledging limitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate lattice structures (triangular/kagome) and show momentum-space bond-current susceptibilities for the square lattice, alongside real-space current configurations demonstrating both closed loops and source–sink patterns.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives form factors for different lattices, calculates susceptibility maxima to predict ordering vectors, and then reconstructs the corresponding real-space current topology based on these fluctuations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter charge order, the rigorous mathematical framework linking momentum-space susceptibilities to real-space topological currents is highly relevant to understanding emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
